title: Simpson's Paradox Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Statistics
AP Statistics
Simpson's Paradox
Lurking Variable
Conditional Proportions
Aggregated Data
description: Bar chart explorer that compares combined success rates with rates separated by subgroup so students can see when and why Simpson's Paradox reverses a conclusion.

learningObjectives: Evaluate combined and subgroup comparisons to decide whether Simpson's Paradox is present (Evaluate)
Determine which analysis is more appropriate when a lurking variable affects both group membership and the outcome (Evaluate)
Explain how unequal subgroup sizes can reverse a comparison when data are aggregated (Analyze)

keyQuestions: Do the two groups have the same mix of subgroups?
Which comparison answers the question you care about?
commonMisconceptions: The combined data are always more trustworthy because the sample is larger
Simpson's Paradox means one of the calculations is wrong
The paradox can occur even when both groups have the same mix of subgroups
assessmentOpportunities: Student correctly computes a combined rate from the subgroup counts
Student identifies the lurking variable and explains its link to both group and outcome
Student constructs a new set of slider values that produces the paradox
